_meta.purpose: Machine-readable registry of every external source this project relies on. src/stokengineer/provenance.py refuses to use a source id that is not in here, and tools/check_links.py re-checks every URL.

verification_legend.fetched_live: This session opened the URL with the fetch_page tool on 2026-09-22 and read the quoted content.
verification_legend.github_api: This session queried the GitHub REST API (gh api) on 2026-09-22 for repository metadata / release assets.
verification_legend.carried_over: Present in a previous session's registry. NOT re-fetched in this session. Treated as unverified until checked again; nothing in the engine depends on it.

_meta.rules_engine_note: Only entries with official: true feed the rules engine (scoring + roster). Everything else is data plumbing or context and every entry is labelled with its basis.

sources.title: FanDuel rules page does not publish roster shapes or salary caps
sources.what_it_provides: Negative result that matters: as of 2026-09-22 the official FanDuel rules page documents scoring only. There is no public official FanDuel page stating the classic roster shapes (QB/RB/RB/WR/WR/WR/TE/FLEX/DEF) or the $60,000 cap. fanduel.com/nfl-guide now redirects to FanDuel Research. Those values are therefore marked verified:third-party in src/data/roster_rules.json.

sources.title: Stokastic pricing and product FAQ
sources.what_it_provides: All-Access price points shown with the Stokastic avatar toggle on (Core $229.95/mo, Max $349.95/mo, MVP $599.95/mo) and the contest-level simulation claim: 'Game level simulation tools exist on the market currently to help users with projecting player performance. However, nowhere else do users have the ability to perform simulations on the contest level'. Also the tier lineup limits (Core 2K; Max 5K NBA/MLB/CFB, 10K NFL/NASCAR/PGA/NHL classic, 50K NFL showdown; MVP 25K classic, 50K showdown).

sources.title: Stokastic Review 2026 (written by Stokastic)
sources.what_it_provides: Sim mechanics: 'the Sims simulate the contest itself tens of thousands of times: every player's outcome varies sim to sim, correlations hold (a QB's big game drags his receivers up with him), and projected ownership determines how many entrants you are sharing each player with. Every lineup that comes out is then ranked by simulated ROI against the real payout structure of the contest you tell it you are entering.' Also documents the percent-to-first setting, custom projection/ownership CSV upload, Late Swap ('re-rank your live lineups after the early games lock'), and sport-specific 2026 pricing (NFL Core $149.95/mo, Max $229.95/mo, MVP $349.95/mo).

sources.title: NBA DFS Boom Bust: Read Ceiling And Floor Like A Pro
sources.what_it_provides: Boom/Bust definitions used by this engine: ceiling = 75th-percentile outcome, floor = 25th-percentile outcome, Boom = reaching about 5 x (salary/1000) + 10 fantasy points, Bust = falling short of 5 x (salary/1000); worked examples ($9,000 player clears value at ~45 and booms at ~55; $4,000 punt at ~20 and ~30). Also states that in basketball player-to-player correlation barely matters, and that Stokastic does not use Contest Sims for cash games.

sources.title: How To Use NBA DFS Projections To Build Better Lineups
sources.what_it_provides: The two salary metrics this engine implements: Pts/$ = FP / Salary x 1000 (worked example 55 FP at $10,000 = 5.5) and Value = FP - (Salary / 1000 x 5) (worked example 55 - 50 = 5.0; the $5,800 guard at 32 FP = 3.0). Also: minutes come first, usage = share of a team's possessions a player finishes with a shot, a trip to the line, or a turnover, and same-day injury news is the biggest edge.

sources.title: MLB Stats API (official, keyless)
sources.what_it_provides: Official MLB game data: schedules, live feeds, box scores, and player season stats. Keyless. Verified live this session: the call above returned the real 2026-09-21 slate with gamePk 824787 (Blue Jays at Orioles) final 3-4. The response carries an MLB copyright notice pointing at http://gdx.mlb.com/components/copyright.txt - read it before redistributing.

sources.title: nflverse-data (open NFL data releases)
sources.publisher: nflverse (open source project, not the NFL)
sources.what_it_provides: Free, no-key NFL datasets published as GitHub release assets: play-by-play (pbp), player stats, schedules (games.csv), snap counts, depth charts, weekly rosters, injuries, Next Gen Stats, FTN charting. Licence confirmed CC-BY-4.0 through the GitHub API this session.

sources.title: nflverse schedules/games.csv release asset
sources.what_it_provides: One row per NFL game with teams, date/time, roof, surface, spread/total where available. Asset name verified through the GitHub API this session (tag 'schedules' exposes games.csv, games.csv.gz, games.parquet, games.qs, games.rds, timestamp.json).

sources.title: nflverse player_stats release asset
sources.what_it_provides: Per-player per-week NFL stat lines (used to build the empirical game-to-game variance and covariance the models are calibrated against). Asset naming verified via the GitHub API this session (player_stats_YYYY.csv / .csv.gz / .parquet / .qs / .rds).
sources.provides: current-season weekly player stats (touchdowns, yards, receptions, attempts, targets, fantasy points) as CSV; the older `player_stats` tag only carries regular season aggregates up to 2024
sources.notes: Asset list verified through the GitHub releases API on 2026-09-22: the `stats_player` tag's week-2025 asset exists (the fetch redirects to it), while the `player_stats` tag publishes nothing for 2025 (only season aggregates through 2024), so the old pattern was a 404. The dead URL was caught by tools/check_links.py in CI, fixed here, and code and ledger are now asserted to agree in tests/test_ingest.py.

sources.title: nflverse injuries release asset
sources.what_it_provides: Weekly NFL injury report statuses (used as the context layer for availability adjustments). Asset naming verified via the GitHub API this session (injuries_YYYY.csv and parquet/qs/rds).

sources.title: nba_api - Python client for stats.nba.com
sources.publisher: swar (community), wrapping the official NBA stats endpoints
sources.what_it_provides: Free, no-key access to the NBA's own stats endpoints (league dashboards, box scores, play-by-play). MIT licensed (confirmed via GitHub API this session). The upstream NBA endpoints are rate limited and occasionally flaky; the ingest layer caches and backs off.

sources.title: ESPN public scoreboard/odds feed
sources.what_it_provides: Keyless JSON for games, venues, scores and (where posted) betting odds including spread and total - the free path to implied team totals. Verified live this session: returned the real 2026 NFL regular season week 2 with Buffalo 41 - Detroit (2026-09-18). Not an official league API and not documented as a public API; use politely and cache.
sources.licence_or_terms: ESPN terms; undocumented public endpoint. Flagged as best-effort.

sources.title: DraftKings public lobby JSON
sources.what_it_provides: Keyless JSON listing live contests with entry fee (a), max entries (mec), prize pool (po) and the draft group id (dg) needed to pull that slate's player pool. Verified live this session (returned real NFL contests for the 2026-09-20 main slate, draft group 153769). This is an undocumented public endpoint; DraftKings' terms may restrict automated access. The engine treats it as best-effort and always accepts a user-supplied CSV instead.
sources.licence_or_terms: DraftKings site terms; automated access may be restricted - flagged as an irregularity.

sources.title: Stokastic home page
sources.what_it_provides: Product surface: projections, ownership, sims; links the tool suite (DataHub, Contest Generator, Pre-Contest Simulator, Single Lineup Simulator, Post-Contest Simulator, Late Swap) at tools.stokastic.com.

sources.title: DFS Boom Bust probability (general)
sources.what_it_provides: General statement that a projection is the middle of a range and that Stokastic pairs each projection with a modelled range (standard deviation, ceiling, floor, Boom%, Bust%).

sources.title: MLB DFS ownership projections
sources.what_it_provides: Ownership is a forecast of the percentage of tournament entries that will roster a player (i.e. a forecast of opponent behaviour), and chalk is driven by Vegas over/unders, implied run totals, ballparks and pitching matchups.

sources.title: How to use MLB DFS data (DataHub columns)
sources.what_it_provides: DataHub column set (Name, Team, Salary, Position, Order, projected FP, Value, projected ownership) and the Top Stacks tool: team-level stacks with projected stack total, stack ownership and how often the stack lands in optimal lineups.

sources.title: NFL DFS defense strategy (implied team totals)
sources.what_it_provides: The implied team total arithmetic implemented in rules.py: total/2 + spread/2 for the favourite, total/2 - spread/2 for the underdog (worked example 44 total with -7 giving 25.5 and 18.5).

sources.title: Stokastic projection system (OddsShopper, Stokastic's betting arm)
sources.what_it_provides: Description of the projection system as simulation-driven rather than a rating built off last season's box scores.

sources.title: Accurately predicting NBA minutes (RotoGrinders lesson)
sources.what_it_provides: Third-party minutes heuristic used as the NBA minutes prior: 240 team minutes per game, baseline blending season minutes with recent minutes, and a blowout haircut as the spread grows. Not a Stokastic source and not official; labelled as an external prior.

sources.title: Interview with Alex 'Awesemo' Baker
sources.what_it_provides: Founder background (Washington University in St. Louis, professional poker, DFS).

sources.title: Alex Baker on X
sources.what_it_provides: Self-described ranking history ('2017-2021 #1 ranked overall for daily fantasy') and Stokastic cofounder status. Social profile: not machine-checkable, treat as a claim by the person, not a verified statistic.

sources.title: Third-party Stokastic review (2026)
sources.what_it_provides: Independent commentary on tiers/price increases and the absence of a free trial. Third-party opinion, not evidence about Stokastic's internals.

sources.title: The Odds API (optional, key required)
sources.what_it_provides: Odds aggregation across books with a free monthly request quota. REQUIRES A SIGN-UP KEY, so per this project's rules it is optional only: nothing in the default pipeline calls it, and the keyless ESPN feed is the default odds path.
